What this run surfaced

Area clustering looks right

Tamia's sub-zones (Castle, Town Center, Local, Wharves, Deeps, Eastern/Western) pull tight together; distant wilderness (Grey Mountains, Arctic Glaciers, the Great Desert) sit far apart — matching real travel volume rather than a fixed layout.

Shrines correctly isolated

All three Arnakian Shrine areas (Knowledge, Power, Strength) sit in their own strip below the main map with zero connecting lines, per instruction — they're portal-only in the game too.

Bent, obstacle-avoiding connectors

Area-to-area links now route as orthogonal (bent) lines anchored to each area's actual entry floor, detouring around other areas' panels instead of cutting straight through them — 96.8% of all connector pairs (4,791/4,950) don't cross each other at all, down from a much messier baseline. A placement pass also actively swaps area positions when doing so removes line crossings.

Not every crossing is eliminated

With 100 links among 59 areas, a handful of crossings are geometrically unavoidable without much more elaborate routing (or more space) — the remainder are flagged in the render script's own crossing count for anyone who wants to push further; area-to-area geographic direction ("Grey Mountains is north of Tamia") still isn't modeled, since the logs mostly don't carry reliable compass data between distant areas.

Full corpus: 1,436 files in Olmran/logs/action. Pipeline: parse_logs.py → per-area grid_layout.py → macro_layout.py (force-directed area placement) → render_map.py.
